Subject: Tenant-specific log sanitization and CAIQ evidence request

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our InfoSec reviewers raised a couple of follow-ups related to customer-scoped logs and redaction:

- Can Redwood provide a short description of how tenant-scoped logs are sanitized before archival? We need to understand the steps (masking vs. truncation), where it happens in the pipeline, and which log classes are affected (request/response traces, debug events, runtime metrics).
- For CAIQ/SIG controls about data minimization and deletion, your team indicated you can provide supplemental material — specifically mapping to CAIQ questions around logging and deletion proof. Will you be able to supply a control-mapped spreadsheet and a short attestation of the deletion workflow?

We also have one practical ask: our legal team would like an example redaction artifact (redacted log snippet) for a single tenant (no PII included in the sample) and a short write-up of expected delivery timeframe.

Can you loop in whoever owns the SOC2 deletion workflow and the CAIQ pack? We want to slot this into our security review this week.

Best,
Cynthia Park
Head of Information Security
HelioPharm

Subject: Re: Tenant-specific log sanitization and CAIQ evidence request

Cynthia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (security) and Rishi (legal/ops) to pull the artifacts. High-level answers below, and we will follow up with the spreadsheet and a short redaction sample by EOD tomorrow if that works.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Tenant-scoped logs: we segregate logs at ingestion — tenant-id is part of the routing metadata. Redaction is applied in the processing layer before any archival export.
- Redaction approach: default is deterministic masking for known PII fields (email, SSN-like patterns), token truncation for large unstructured blobs, and field-level redaction rules for request/response payloads.
- Classes: request/response traces and application-level debug events are sanitized. Runtime metrics (CPU, GPU utilization, throughput) are retained as-is and are tenant-scoped metrics without customer content.

Next steps we propose:
1) Neha will attach a short redaction playbook (controls and examples) + CAIQ mapping.
2) Rishi will confirm what we can provide as an attestation vs. what requires legal signature/processing.
3) Deliverables: redaction-playbook.pdf, caiq-supplemental-answers.xlsx, and an annotated SOC2 deletion-process PDF.

If you prefer a quick 30-min sync to accelerate, happy to schedule — suggest Thu 6/3 10:00am PT.

Thanks —
Ben Carter

Cynthia — thanks for the signal. I own the technical controls side; attaching the short artifacts we discussed. Please find the included stubs and notes below.

Attachment stubs included here:
- redaction-playbook.pdf — executive summary + examples (deterministic masking, regex patterns, field-level allowlist/denylist).
- caiq-supplemental-answers.xlsx — CAIQ question IDs, Redwood control references, steps to reproduce deletion proof artifacts.
- soc2-deletion-process-annotated.pdf — annotated excerpt of our SOC2 deletion and evidence handling process (redacted for third-party confidentiality).

Key technical notes:
- Where redaction runs: redaction executes in the streaming processing tier (before any Index/Archive write). That tier is a service boundary located in the same tenant-scoped namespace; we never write raw request/response payloads to long-term object storage.
- Cache/ephemeral tokens: KV caches used for inference are in-memory and evicted according to per-tenant TTLs; snapshots are not taken for these caches by default.
- Forensics & proof-of-delete: we can provide a time-stamped metadata record showing the redaction job run id, object identifiers, and deletion markers. The actual provenance artifact is a signed manifest from our retention service — we can export a customer-limited manifest for HelioPharm.

Scope/limitations (so expectations are clear):
- We can produce redaction sample snippets for a single tenant as a demonstration artifact (no PII).
- Full-scale production proofs across all tenants require an operational runbook request and will follow our SOC2 evidence handling workflow (may take 7-10 business days to assemble and sign).

We will upload the two working files to the shared drive and send the DocuSign/attestation checkbox language that Rishi will coordinate with Legal.

Neha Kapoor
